grade.first_issue: In the odd-degree case, the claim that the minimum exponent over all \(k\le n\) equals \(2-n\) is false: \(k=n-1\) gives exponent \(1-n\). Nevertheless, this is still greater than \(-n\), so the required contradiction remains valid.
grade.summary: The coefficient analysis correctly determines all solutions as \(P(x)=x^2\) and \(P(x)=x^4+ax^2+6\). The sole defect is a localized incorrect minimum-exponent statement in excluding odd degrees, readily repaired by observing that every exponent occurring on the right is greater than \(-n\).
strengths: Correctly expands the averaging operator on every monomial.
Handles degrees \(0\) through \(4\) explicitly and obtains the correct coefficients.
The \(x^{n-4}\)-coefficient comparison correctly excludes every even degree greater than \(4\).

errors.description: The stated minimum exponent for odd \(n>4\) overlooks the contribution from \(k=n-1\), although the corrected bound still proves that \(x^{-n}\) cannot occur.
